videos.title: Button States 101
videos.why: Enabled, disabled, focus, hover and selected states in three minutes, with what each one has to tell the user; list which of them your own primary button is missing.

videos.title: Why Disabled Buttons Hurt UX (and How to Fix Them)
videos.why: Why a greyed-out button that does nothing confuses people; note at 0:43 that contrast rules do not cover disabled controls, then copy the three tips at 3:01 into your component checklist.

podcasts.episode: Fab Components: Bethany Fong on Designing Material's Signature Floating Action Button
podcasts.why: The story of a single component, Material's floating action button, from a designer who helped create Material Design; listen for how much thinking sits behind one round button.

podcasts.episode: 84: Interface elements with too much responsibility
podcasts.why: Each host picks interface elements that do more jobs than they should; good practice for asking what any one component in your app is actually responsible for.

reads.title: Button States: Communicate Interaction
reads.why: The written companion to the video, with an example of each state; use it as the checklist when you work through lab-states.

reads.title: States
reads.why: Google's six interaction states (enabled, disabled, hover, focused, pressed, dragged) and the note that states use two visual indicators for accessibility; a quick standard to compare your components against.

reads.title: Toggle Buttons
reads.why: Builds an accessible toggle step by step, showing that a component's state has to exist in the code (aria-pressed) as well as in how it looks; the bridge between a designed state and a built one.
